column2: Several banks depend on the same vulnerable wholesale lender. Which Bank of England committee examines the system-wide risk?
column7: The FPC considers risks that spread through links between institutions. The Monetary Policy Committee sets monetary policy.

column2: Who appoints the chair of the Financial Conduct Authority under FSMA?
column7: Schedule 1ZA assigns the chair's appointment to the Treasury. Other board seats have different appointment arrangements.

column2: Which UK body reviews proposed mergers that could leave customers with too few suppliers?
column7: The CMA reviews qualifying mergers and can require the parties to take measures while it investigates.

column2: Who enforces an employer's duty to enrol eligible staff in a workplace pension?
column7: The Pensions Regulator checks that employers enrol qualifying staff and pay contributions. Resolving a member's dispute is a different function.

column2: Which issue falls within the PRA's remit when it supervises a building society?
column5: Accuracy of its annual tax return
column7: The PRA examines a building society's financial resilience, including whether it can meet withdrawals. The FCA supervises its business conduct.

column2: What does Parliament establish for the FCA through legislation?
column7: Parliament sets the FCA's objectives and the boundaries of its responsibilities. The regulator exercises its powers within those boundaries.

column2: Which document does the FCA use to report its yearly performance to the Treasury?
column7: The annual report explains how the FCA has pursued its objectives. A decision notice concerns a particular case.

column2: Banks face losses and are cutting lending. Which FPC action releases capital built up against cyclical risks?
column7: The FPC can release the countercyclical buffer so banks can absorb losses while continuing to lend.

column2: Which instrument specifies kinds of investment for the general definition in section 22 of FSMA?
column7: Section 22 gives the Treasury the power to specify kinds of activity and investment by order.

column2: A firm lacks authorisation for a UK regulated activity. Which status can satisfy the general prohibition?
column7: Section 19 allows an authorised or exempt person to carry on a regulated activity. Company registration alone confers neither status.

column2: Which feature does the general FSMA definition require for an activity involving a specified investment?
column3: Carried on by way of business
column4: Carried on solely for retail clients
column7: Section 22 asks whether the specified activity is carried on by way of business. The client's retail status is not part of that general test.

column2: How did EU market abuse rules become part of the UK's domestic regime on leaving the EU?
column4: Replacement by a stock exchange code
column7: The EU (Withdrawal) Act brought the regulation into UK law. Amendments adapted it for the domestic market.

column2: Which aim is the FCA's strategic objective under FSMA?
column7: The strategic objective concerns how the markets work. Consumer protection, integrity and competition are operational objectives.

column2: Whose interests guide the FCA when it promotes effective competition?
column7: The FCA promotes rivalry between firms for the benefits it can bring customers, such as better services or prices.

column2: A new FCA rule would help UK firms expand abroad. Which objective makes this consideration relevant?
column5: Integrity of the UK financial system
column6: Competition in the interests of consumers
column7: The secondary objective concerns the UK economy's competitiveness and growth over the medium to long term. It operates alongside the primary objectives when the FCA makes rules.

column2: Can the FCA use its secondary growth objective to reduce a penalty on an individual exporter it regulates?
column3: No, the decision concerns one firm
column4: Yes, if its overseas business is material
column5: No, the objective covers domestic trade only
column6: Yes, if the firm retains its permission
column7: The secondary objective shapes the FCA's general functions, such as rule-making. It does not apply to an individual enforcement decision.

column2: Where does the FCA obtain its funding for day-to-day supervision?
column7: The FCA funds its operations through regulatory fees. Accountability to Parliament does not mean it relies on a general tax grant.

column2: Which PRA objective applies specifically to its supervision of insurers?
column7: The PRA has a specific objective concerning insurance customers as well as its general safety and soundness objective.

column2: When a major bank fails, which interest explains the PRA's support for orderly resolution?
column4: Continuity of the bank's legal structure
column6: Preservation of the bank's market share
column7: Disruption to payments and lending can spread to households and other firms. The PRA and the Bank of England plan for the effect on these services.

column2: A bank writes down a loan portfolio. Which resource can absorb those losses while it trades on?
column7: Ordinary shares and reserves provide capital that can absorb losses while a bank continues operating. Deposits and ordinary borrowing are liabilities.

column2: A bank has valuable long-term assets but cannot meet today's withdrawals. Which risk has materialised?
column7: Liquidity concerns access to cash when needed. Holding assets of value does not ensure the bank can turn them into cash in time.

column2: When assessing liquidity, why does the PRA examine where a banking group holds its cash?
column6: Group capital expires at year end
column7: A group may have ample cash overall while one subsidiary cannot access it during stress. The assessment considers availability at the entity that needs it.

column2: What should a life insurer use to test its financial projections under stress?
column5: Forecasts based on the average year
column7: The PRA expects insurers to explore adverse scenarios and assess whether their cash flows and solvency would hold up.

column2: Which action can help an insurer rebuild capital internally after a shock?
column7: Cutting distributions leaves more resources in the insurer. Moving cash between its own accounts does not generate capital.

column2: How long must a deposit-taker continue to satisfy the PRA's threshold conditions?
column7: Threshold conditions govern continued permission as well as entry. The PRA assesses firms against them on an ongoing basis.

column2: Which factor best explains why the PRA assigns different levels of scrutiny to two banks?
column4: Profit growth achieved by each bank
column5: Market share gained in the last quarter
column6: Time elapsed since each bank's last audit
column7: The PRA prioritises the risks to its objectives, including the disruption a bank could cause. A change in profit or market share alone does not measure that impact.

column2: Which analysis would help a supervisor assess a bank's resilience to sudden deposit withdrawals?
column4: Loan losses after a house price fall
column5: Bond values after an interest rate rise
column7: A liquidity stress test examines whether the bank could meet payments as cash leaves. The other analyses address credit, market or operational exposures.

column2: Which regulator supervises the financial resources of an investment adviser authorised solely by the FCA?
column7: The FCA provides prudential supervision for firms it alone authorises. The PRA supervises banks, insurers and certain other institutions.

column2: How does the FCA usually group firms into portfolios for supervision?
column7: Firms earning revenue in similar ways can give rise to similar risks. Grouping them helps the FCA compare those risks.

column2: Why might a supervisor scrutinise a firm's heavy reliance on sales bonuses?
column7: The way a firm rewards staff can encourage sales at the expense of customer needs. The FCA considers commercial incentives when assessing potential harm.

column2: What determines whether the FCA may assign dedicated oversight to a firm alongside portfolio supervision?
column3: Scale of potential harm to customers or markets
column4: Number of years with the same supervisor
column6: Number of permissions held at authorisation
column7: The FCA may dedicate resources to firms with the greatest potential impact. Firms sharing a business model are generally supervised in a portfolio.

column2: An authorised adviser wants to enter a regulated line of business beyond its remit. What should it seek?
column7: The scope of permission must cover the activity. The firm must wait for approval before starting the new business.

column2: Where does an authorised finance firm apply to add permission to accept deposits?
column7: The PRA handles applications to add deposit-taking. Existing authorisation for another business line does not cover it.

column2: What defines the business an appointed representative can carry out for its principal?
column7: The agreement specifies the permitted work. The principal must take reasonable steps to keep the representative within that scope.

column2: Which activity can an introducer appointed representative carry out for its principal?
column7: An introducer may make introductions and distribute permitted promotions. Personal recommendations go beyond that limited role.

column2: Who oversees a representative's regulated work under its written appointment?
column7: The principal takes responsibility for this business and needs resources to supervise it. Appointment does not transfer oversight to the representative's accountant.

column2: A principal's appointed representative expands into more complex work. Which assessment addresses the resulting oversight risk?
column5: Advisers' eligibility for an annual SPS
column7: A principal needs people and controls suited to the work it oversees. Checking customer suitability or advisers' qualifications alone does not establish that capacity.

column2: Which document evidences a retail investment adviser's qualifications, ethics declaration and continuing development?
column7: The SPS records verification by an accredited body. A statement describing a manager's responsibilities serves a different purpose.

column2: An adviser has a current SPS. Who still assesses competence for the role?
column7: The certificate is evidence of professional standing. The firm's own responsibility to assess competence continues.

column2: What distinguishes structured continuing professional development from general professional reading?
column7: Structured learning has a specific goal. It can take place online or in-house and does not require a formal examination.

column2: A retail investment adviser logs 24 structured CPD hours and 8 unstructured hours. How many more hours reach the annual minimum?
column7: These activities total 32 hours. The FCA requires 35 overall for retail investment activities and the adviser already exceeds the 21 structured hours.

column2: An adviser seeks an SPS without joining the issuing accredited body. What does the FCA require?
column7: Accredited bodies verify advisers' qualifications and professional standards. Membership of the issuing body is optional.

column2: Which FCA sourcebook contains the rules on promotions for retail investments?
column7: The FCA directs firms to COBS for investment promotions. ICOBS deals with general insurance and BCOBS with banking.

column2: A broker moves an investment advert from print to social media. Which standard applies?
column6: The standard for general insurance adverts
column7: The FCA's requirement for clear, fair and non-misleading promotions applies across media. Changing the channel does not change the product rules.

column2: Where should a viewer complain about an investment campaign's taste and decency?
column7: The FCA directs complaints about taste and decency to the ASA. Concerns about misleading financial claims can go to the FCA.

column2: What determines a firm's size classification under the FCA's CASS regime?
column7: FCA classification reflects the scale of client money or custody assets held. The firm's own capital is a different measure.

column2: Which document helps an insolvency practitioner locate an investment firm's customer holdings promptly?
column7: The CASS resolution pack brings together the records needed to return client assets after failure.

column2: Which record belongs in the CASS resolution pack for a firm holding customers' securities?
column7: Custodian details help the insolvency practitioner trace where investments are held. The pack also covers relevant reconciliations.

column2: A firm indexes existing records in its CASS resolution pack. Which event must its retrieval arrangements accommodate?
column4: Publication of the firm's annual accounts
column5: Completion of its regulatory reporting cycle
column7: The pack must allow prompt access to the records after the firm fails as well as during normal business. An index that depends on the firm continuing to trade is insufficient.

column2: A broker will hold client money before it first takes custody of securities. When must its CASS resolution pack be ready?
column5: At the first external CASS audit
column7: Holding client money under CASS 7 already triggers the pack requirement. Taking custody of securities later does not postpone it.

column2: What filing gives the FCA a monthly view of a CASS medium firm's customer holdings?
column7: The CMAR reports client money and safe custody assets. The annual classification exercise has a different purpose.

column2: Which information about a listed company is most likely to satisfy the UK MAR definition of inside information?
column3: Private confirmation of a material takeover
column4: Published audited turnover for last year
column7: The information must be precise, non-public and likely to affect the price significantly. A confirmed material deal can meet those tests.

column2: A trader cancels an order after learning privately of a material takeover. What breach arises from using that news?
column7: Using inside information to amend or cancel an existing order falls within insider dealing even without a completed purchase.

column2: A director privately tells a friend price-sensitive inside information outside her duties. Which UK MAR prohibition applies?
column7: Passing inside information outside the normal exercise of one's duties can breach UK MAR, even without an order to trade.

column2: What allows a firm to test investor interest before a potential transaction under UK MAR safeguards?
column7: The market sounding framework provides a route for legitimate disclosures if its safeguards are met.

column2: Which condition prevents a listed issuer delaying disclosure of inside information under the ordinary UK MAR test?
column7: Delay requires confidentiality, a legitimate interest in delaying and no likelihood of misleading the public. Losing confidentiality removes a necessary condition.

column2: An issuer lawfully delayed publishing inside information under the ordinary rule. When does it notify the FCA?
column4: Before the board first considers delay
column5: On completion of its annual audit
column6: At the next scheduled results announcement
column7: The issuer notifies the FCA when it has made the information public and retains its reasons in case they are requested.

column2: A listed issuer's employee sees its price-sensitive results before publication. Where must the issuer record her access?
column7: UK MAR requires the issuer to list its own staff who have access to inside information. Service providers acting on its behalf can have separate list obligations.

column2: A UK trading venue suspects manipulation through unexecuted orders. What should it submit to the FCA?
column4: Monthly client money and asset return
column5: Failure notification under the CASS rules
column6: Suspicious activity report to the NCA
column7: The STOR regime covers orders and attempted abuse. An executed trade is unnecessary, and a money laundering report serves a separate regime.

column2: What evidence threshold triggers a UK broker's STOR duty for a trade it arranges?
column7: The broker reports suspected market abuse without delay once reasonable grounds exist. The FCA investigates whether a breach occurred.

column2: A broker spots unusual trading it did not arrange and lacks the detail for a STOR. Which FCA route can it use?
column7: The FCA accepts market observations about activity that falls outside the observer's STOR reporting obligation.

column2: Which FCA sanction formally criticises a firm's misconduct without imposing a fine?
column7: Public censure records formal criticism. It is a separate sanction from a financial penalty or criminal prosecution.

column2: Which FCA measure can prevent an individual from performing specified functions in regulated business?
column7: Prohibition restricts the individual's functions. Measures affecting the firm do not necessarily bar the individual from working elsewhere.

column2: Which FCA notice invites representations before a proposed disciplinary measure is decided?
column7: A warning notice explains proposed action and gives the recipient a chance to respond before a decision.

column2: A broker disputes an FCA disciplinary decision notice. Where can it refer the matter?
column7: The statutory reference is to the Upper Tribunal. The Ombudsman deals with consumer complaints about firms.

column2: Which notice follows when a firm accepts the FCA's disciplinary decision and the reference period expires?
column7: The FCA gives a final notice after the decision stage if there is no tribunal reference within the relevant period.

column2: A firm receives notice that a specialist will examine its controls under section 166. Who can make this appointment directly?
column7: Section 166 allows the regulator to appoint the author itself or require the firm to provide a report.

column2: A regulator directs a firm to appoint a specialist under section 166. Who must approve or nominate the specialist?
column7: Where the firm makes the appointment, the regulator must nominate or approve a person with the necessary skills.

column2: What must an outsourced provider do when a section 166 reviewer examines work it performed for a firm?
column7: The duty extends to people who provide or previously provided services connected with the matter under review.

column2: A product works as designed but reaches customers outside its intended market. Which Consumer Duty outcome is at issue?
column7: The product outcome concerns who a product is designed and distributed for. Sound design alone cannot make the distribution suitable.

column2: A firm cuts its fee but removes useful cover. What comparison tests fair value under the Consumer Duty?
column4: New fee against last year's fee
column7: A lower price alone does not establish value. The firm must consider what customers receive for the price they pay.

column2: Which finding best demonstrates the Consumer Duty outcome for understanding a retail investment communication?
column3: Readers can explain the main risk
column6: Investors chose the most popular fund
column7: Comprehension testing shows whether customers can use the information to make decisions. Delivery or readership alone does not establish understanding.
